physics_goals.locator: History of Neutrinos at Lab E
physics_goals.quote: Among the most important results were measurements of the structure of the proton and the electroweak mixing angle.
physics_goals.value: Measure deep-inelastic neutrino-nucleon scattering: the structure of the proton, the strange-quark content, charm production and the electroweak mixing angle

summary.plain: A series of Fermilab experiments in the 1980s in which a 690-tonne iron-and-scintillator detector recorded high-energy neutrinos from the Tevatron, used to measure how quarks are distributed inside the proton and to test the electroweak theory. Its detector was later reused by NuTeV.
summary.technical: Chicago-Columbia-Fermilab-Rochester neutrino experiments (E616 1979, E701 1982, E744 1985, E770 1987-88) at Fermilab Lab E: 690 t unmagnetised steel-scintillator target calorimeter with drift chambers followed by a toroidal muon spectrometer in a quadrupole-triplet wide-band muon-neutrino/antineutrino beam of 800 GeV protons (E up to ~600 GeV); structure functions F2 and xF3, strange-sea and charm (kappa, |V_cd|), sin^2(theta_W) and alpha_s.
